translations.text: These are the words that Baruch son of Neriah sent to the nine and a half tribes who were beyond the Euphrates River. The following was written in the letter:
Thus says Baruch son of Neriah to the brothers who were taken captive: Mercy and peace.
I remember, my brothers, the love of the one who led us, who loved us from long ago and never hated us, but rather disciplined us all the more.
And I know for certain that all twelve of us tribes are bound together by one bond, since we were born of one father.

For this reason I have been especially concerned to leave you the words of this letter before I die, so that you may be comforted concerning the troubles that have reached you, and may also grieve over the disaster that befell your brothers. You should also acknowledge the justice of the judgment of the one who decreed that you should be taken captive. For what you have suffered is less than what you have done, so that in the last times you may be found worthy of your fathers.

Therefore, if you consider that you have suffered these things now for your own good, so that you will not be judged and tormented at the end, then you will receive an everlasting hope—if you completely remove from your hearts the empty delusion because of which you went away from here.

For if you do these things in this way, he will continually remember you—the one who has always promised on our behalf to those greater than us that he would not forget us or abandon us forever, but would gather the scattered again with great mercy.
Now, my brothers, you already know what happened to Zion: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against us.
For we sinned against him who made us and did not keep the commandment he gave us.
But what happened to you also overtook us, so that we should suffer still more. For it happened to us too.

And now, my brothers, I am telling you that when the enemies surrounded the city, angels of the Most High were sent. They demolished the fortifications of the mighty wall and shattered the strong iron corners that could not be uprooted.
But they hid some of the sacred vessels so that they would not be defiled by the enemies.

After doing these things, they handed over to the enemies the demolished wall, the plundered house, the burned temple, and the people who had been defeated because they had been handed over. This was so that the enemies would not boast and say, ‘We have proved so strong that we have even destroyed the house of the Most High in battle.’
They also bound your brothers and took them to Babylon, and settled them there.
Only a very few of us were left here.
This is the distress about which I have written to you.
For I know for certain that, as long as you knew Zion was prospering, her inhabited state comforted you more than your distance from her distressed you.
But hear a word of comfort as well.
For I was mourning over Zion and asking the Most High for mercy, and I said:
For how long will these things remain with us, and troubles keep coming upon us?

These things the Mighty One has done according to his abundant mercy, and the Most High according to the greatness of his compassion. He revealed a message to me so that I might be comforted, and showed me a vision so that I would no longer grieve. He made known to me the mystery of the times and showed me the coming of the appointed seasons.
For this reason, my brothers, I have written to you, so that you may find comfort from your many troubles.

But know that our Maker will certainly exact vengeance for us from all our enemies, according to everything they have done to us. Moreover, the end that the Most High will bring about is very near, and his mercies are coming. The completion of his judgment is not far away.
For look, we now see the great prosperity of the nations, even though they act wickedly. But they are like a breath.
We look at the vastness of their dominion, though they act unjustly. But they will be like a drop of water.
We see how firmly established their power is, even though they continually stand against the Mighty One. But they will be regarded as spittle.
We consider their glorious greatness, even though they do not keep the commandments of the Most High. But they will pass away like smoke.
We reflect on the beauty of their lives, even though they conduct themselves in uncleanness. But they will wither like grass in the heat.
We consider the strength of their cruelty, even though they give no thought to the end. But they will be shattered like a passing wave.
We contemplate the splendor of their power, even though they deny the goodness of the one who gave it to them. But they will pass away like a passing cloud.
For the Most High is surely hastening his times and bringing his appointed seasons.
And he will certainly judge those who are in his world, and will truly call everything to account according to all their secret deeds.
He will certainly examine hidden thoughts and everything stored in the secret chamber of every part of a human being, and will bring it into the open before everyone with rebuke.
Therefore, do not let any of these present things occupy your hearts. Instead, let us wait all the more eagerly, because what he promised us is coming.
And let us not look now at the luxury of the nations, but remember what has been promised to us at the end.
For the limits of the times and seasons are surely passing away, together with everything in them.
At the end of the world, its ruler will display his great power, when everything comes to judgment.
You, therefore, set your hearts firmly on what you believed from the beginning, so that you are not shut out of both worlds: you have now been taken captive, and you would then be tormented as well.
For among all things that exist now, that have passed, or that are coming, neither is evil fully evil, nor is good completely good.
For all present health turns into sickness.
And all present might turns into weakness, and all present strength turns into infirmity.
And all the vigor of youth turns to old age and an end. And all the beauty of present loveliness turns dark and hateful.
And all present proud dominion turns into humiliation and shame.
And all the glory of present greatness turns to silent shame. And all present pride and arrogance turn to a silent downfall.
And all present luxury and pleasures turn into worms and decay.
And every present boastful shout turns into dust and silence.
And all present possessions and wealth turn into Sheol alone.
And all the grasping impulses of present desire turn to death against their will. And every desire arising from present passions turns to a judgment of torment.
And all present cunning and trickery turn into rebuke by the truth.
And all the sweetness of present ointments turns into judgment and condemnation.
And all love of falsehood turns into disgrace through truth.
So, while all these things are happening now, does anyone think they will not be called to account?
But the end of everything will come to the truth.

So I have now made this known to you while I am still alive. For I have spoken so that you may learn what is good. For the Mighty One commanded me to admonish you and set before you a few of the decrees of his judgment before I die.
Remember that Moses once called heaven and earth to witness against you and said, “If you transgress the law, you will be scattered; but if you keep it, you will be preserved.”
But he also told you other things when you were together in the wilderness as twelve tribes.
And after his death you pushed them away from you. That is why these things that were foretold have overtaken you.
Now Moses told you before these things happened to you, and here they have happened to you, because you abandoned the law.
And now I too tell you, after you have suffered, that if you obey what has been told you, you will receive from the Mighty One everything that has been set aside and kept for you.
Let this letter be a witness between you and me, so that you may remember the commandments of the Mighty One, and so that I too may breathe freely before the one who sent me.
Remember the law, Zion, the holy land, your brothers, and the covenant of your ancestors. Do not forget the festivals and the Sabbaths.
Pass on this letter and the tradition of the law to your children after you, just as your ancestors passed them on to you.

At all times, continually plead and pray earnestly with all your soul, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you and may not count your many sins, but may remember the uprightness of your ancestors.
For if he does not judge us according to his abundant mercy, woe to all of us who have been born!
Know also that in former times and in the generations of long ago, our ancestors had helpers: righteous people and holy prophets.

We were also in our own land, and they helped us when we sinned. They pleaded for us with the one who made us, because they had confidence in their deeds. And the Mighty One heard their prayer and forgave us.
But now the righteous have been gathered away, and the prophets have fallen asleep. We too have left the land, and Zion has been taken from us. Now we have nothing except the Mighty One and his law.
So if we set our hearts right and put them in order, we will receive everything we have lost, and things many times better than what we have lost.
For what we have lost is perishable, but what we will receive does not perish.
I have also written in this way to our brothers in Babylon, to testify to these same things to them as well.
Let all these things that have been said remain before your eyes at all times, because we still have breath and the power to choose freely.
Moreover, the Most High is patient with us here. He has made known to us what is to come and has not hidden from us what will happen at the end.

Therefore, before he demands his judgment and the fulfillment of what is due to him, let us prepare ourselves to receive rather than to be taken away, to hope rather than to be put to shame, and to rest with our ancestors rather than to be tormented with our enemies.

For the youth of the world has passed, and the vigor of creation has already come to an end. The coming of the times is almost over. The bucket is close to the well, the ship to the harbor, the journey to the city, and life to its end.
So prepare yourselves, so that when you have completed the voyage and stepped off the ship, you may find rest, and not be condemned when you depart.

For when the Most High brings about all these things, there will no longer be any place for repentance, any limit to the times, any extension of the seasons, any change bringing relief, any place for petition, any sending of requests, any receiving of knowledge, any giving of love, any place for remorse, any plea for offenses, any petitions from the ancestors, any prayer from the prophets, or any help from the righteous.
There will be a sentence of destruction there, a road of fire, and a path leading to Gehenna.
Therefore there is one law through one person, one world, and an end for everyone in it.
Then he will give life to those whom he can forgive, and at the same time he will destroy those who are stained with sins.
Therefore, when you receive this letter of mine, read it carefully in your assemblies.
And meditate on it, especially on your days of fasting.
Remember me through this letter, just as I too remember you through it. And may you remain well at all times.
